remaining_concerns: Admissible evidence establishes a segment-specific performance gap in logistics customs triage and that this segment is named in two freight customer commitments.

The governing policy treats that weakness as material because it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; product's non-core label does not resolve materiality in that circumstance.
The release policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch for material limitations affecting named launch use cases.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved at the time of certification.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support overall readiness but do not satisfy the separate disclosure-or-risk-acceptance requirement for a material limitation.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no genuinely new admissible evidence and mostly reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is analytically cleaner, but it does not close the core policy failure. The admissible evidence still shows a 1.3-point miss in logistics customs triage, that the segment is named in two freight customer commitments, that legal review on disclosure remains open, and that policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case. Public model-card and AI risk management guidance support documenting limitations and monitoring, and aggregate readiness plus rehearsal results support overall launch readiness, but neither satisfies the unresolved mandatory internal policy predicate. Because concern accounting leaves every initial specific concern open, the record supports preserving the original noncompliance finding rather than moving to compliant_with_caveats.
